subsystems.name: Extreme adaptive optics
subsystems.role: corrects atmospheric turbulence thousands of times per second so the star image stays sharp.
parts: deformable mirror with thousands of actuators

subsystems.name: Coronagraph
subsystems.role: blocks the bright star so faint companions can be seen beside it.

subsystems.name: Integral field spectrograph
subsystems.role: splits the remaining light into a spectrum at every pixel, giving the planet's colour and temperature.

subsystems.name: Wavefront calibration
subsystems.role: measures and removes the optical errors that the wavefront sensor cannot see.

subsystems.name: Post-processing pipeline
subsystems.role: subtracts the residual stellar halo in software.

buildSteps.title: Design for a specific telescope
buildSteps.detail: The coronagraph, adaptive optics and spectrograph are matched to the telescope's aperture, obstruction and site turbulence.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the deformable mirror
buildSteps.detail: A thin reflective membrane is bonded to thousands of piezo or MEMS actuators and polished to optical quality.

buildSteps.title: Make the coronagraph masks
buildSteps.detail: Focal-plane masks and apodizers are etched or deposited with nanometre precision to suppress starlight at the target wavelength.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the instrument
buildSteps.detail: Optics, detectors and cryogenics are assembled in a clean room and aligned on a vibration-isolated bench.

buildSteps.title: Commission on the telescope
buildSteps.detail: The instrument is mounted at a focus, the AO loop is closed on real stars, and non-common-path aberrations are calibrated.

buildSteps.title: Observe with the star blocked
buildSteps.detail: Deep exposures are taken while the field rotates, so the planet moves relative to the residual starlight.

buildSteps.title: Post-process the data
buildSteps.detail: Reference images and the rotating field are combined to subtract the halo, revealing faint point sources.

buildSteps.title: Extract spectra and orbits
buildSteps.detail: The companion's spectrum gives its temperature and atmosphere, while repeated images give its orbit.

prerequisites.why: They collect enough light to see a planet millions of times fainter than its star.

prerequisites.tech: Deformable mirrors with thousands of actuators
prerequisites.why: They must shape the wavefront finely enough to create a dark hole beside the star.
The planet signal is weak, so every stray electron matters.
Masks must be made to sub-wavelength precision to block starlight without dimming the planet.
The AO loop runs at kilohertz rates, and halo subtraction needs large image archives.

pathway.milestone: ground-based extreme AO instruments on 8-m telescopes image young, self-luminous giant planets and take their spectra
pathway.unlocks: the first atmospheric studies of directly imaged exoplanets.

pathway.milestone: dedicated high-contrast instruments on 30-m class telescopes now under construction
pathway.unlocks: imaging of older, fainter giant planets and possibly large rocky planets.

pathway.milestone: reflected-light spectroscopy of mature planetary systems
pathway.unlocks: comparison of exoplanet atmospheres with those in our Solar System.
direct imaging of Earth-like planets around nearby stars — if starlight suppression improves by another factor of a thousand.
